# Role 3 adversarial review

Ground truth: [Role 3](../roles/03_BACKEND_AND_GOVERNANCE.md), with coherence checked against [IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md](../IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md) and [CHALLENGE_SPECIFICATION.md](../CHALLENGE_SPECIFICATION.md). Review covered the authoritative API, contracts, governance transactions, scoring/ECI, audit, exports and runtime configuration. Review agents corrected findings; the parent independently revisited boundaries and integration evidence.

Acceptance uses explicit partitions: valid actions, every state/action pair, malformed inputs, numeric boundaries, stale versions, identical/conflicting retries, simultaneous writes, provider failures, partial completion, corruption and rollback. Coverage measures executed code; it cannot establish that every possible input combination or defect is absent. The measured final results are recorded below.

## Acceptance and regression matrix

| Role task / requirement | Concrete acceptance and regression evidence | Remaining integration boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R01 human decisions and SMART | `test_decisions.py`, `test_decision_review.py`: full state/action table; AI identity, blank rationale, route/body mismatch, stale revision; nested SMART targets/provenance, zero metric target, valid scope vocabulary and source/target/assumption confirmations. | Role 4 must demonstrate these decisions with actual customer-facing content. Prototype actor inputs are not authentication. |
| R02 transactional revisions/state/rank/turn/audit | `test_neo4j_integration.py`: direct graph snapshots before/after injected decision/application and late materialization failure; one winner for concurrent expected revisions. `test_decision_review.py`: simultaneous application retry and freeze recheck after provider resolution. | Repeat against intended deployment and its actual adapters. |
| R03 overrides | `test_scoring.py`, `test_decision_review.py`: negative, out-of-policy, nonnumeric, bool, NaN/Infinity; explicit zero, calculated/effective distinction, before/after audit; edits clear override. | UI must distinguish zero from disabled override. |
| R04 stable regeneration/revisions | `test_decision_review.py`: order-independent identity, approved/rejected preservation, changed evidence refresh, stale turn cannot resurrect, identical/conflicting retries; explicit legacy import and reviewed reconciliation. | Real engine must supply semantic keys and versioned lineage. |
| R10 provider/runtime | `test_runtime.py`, `test_cli_review.py`: OpenAI-only/Anthropic-only, explicit/auto selection, missing/whitespace keys, pipeline path/config failure and truthful runner checks. | No live provider or complete raw-conversion pipeline demonstrated. |
| R09 API container address | `test_runtime.py` parses Compose provider forwarding and UI `API_BASE_URL=http://api:8000`. | Docker binary and Role 4 UI unavailable; build/health/network acceptance pending. |
| R11 scoped 2030 reach | `test_scoring.py`, `test_scoring_review.py`: golden arithmetic, G60/G68 deduplication, conflicting duplicate facts, source locator structure, wrong year/region exclusion, explicit zero forecast, missing scopes, fixed-reference validation. `test_decision_review.py`: immutable config, explicit required proxy assumption IDs and future derivative mapping. | Role 1 must establish actual source cells, fixed total and proxy semantics. |
| R12 ECI | Golden ECI, distinct traceable support IDs, ID precedence over inflated broad counts, logarithmic cap, native regional coverage, review levels, unknown count range, concentration/contradiction/proposed-target warnings and non-probability semantics in scoring suites. | Actual relevant support and reviewed study mappings are authoritative provider responsibilities. |
| R13/R15 evidence/targets | `test_decision_review.py`: source-backed target linkage, current-source revalidation, uncited strategy provisional/blocking, specific proxy IDs; API review tests reject unverified citations and malformed model patches without writes. Opposition warnings do not increase ECI. | Real mapped studies, strategy passages and model citations remain unintegrated. |
| R16 documented sensitivity | Scoring suites cover all unknown factors, known severity/unknown cohort and known mention/unknown severity, discovery candidate upper bounds, regional proportions rather than pooled counts, finite counts/weights/factors and separate legacy scale. | Synthetic cohort/forecast fixtures do not validate real uncertainty inputs. |
| R18 full payload audit and immutability | `test_audit_export.py`, `test_scoring_review.py`: altered fields, deletion/reorder/full rehash against retained checkpoint, malformed checkpoints/events, reserved metadata, serialization failure atomicity. `test_repository_review.py`: immutable revisions/config/freezes/rankings, candidate consistency, native graph index/copy tampering and coherent reads/writes. API review tests retain import, visible tool/citation, stale review and discarded suggestion history. | Source/consolidation events require actual import adapter outputs. Independently retain checkpoints. |
| R19 complete exports/freeze | Export suites exercise more than 200 rows, required BMW columns populated from actual RequirementDetail fields, Pydantic JSON/CSV roundtrip, empty export and nested arrays. Decision suites cover stale/unapproved freeze, source snapshots, policy reconstruction and immutable later edits. | Verify actual BMW locator/content completeness and private delivery package. |
| Shared API/contracts | `test_api_boundaries.py`, `test_api_review.py`: detail/evidence/history/download, configurable prefix/root aliases, sources/records/PDFs, allowlisted path and symlink escape, requirement/signal threads, partial jobs, adapter progress/cache modes, resource errors, citation resolution, provider faults and lifespan ownership. | Real Role 1/2 contracts and Role 4 client integration remain pending. |

## Findings corrected

- Malformed nested SMART/scope/provenance fields, nonfinite payloads and truthy fake traceability flags could reach governance boundaries. Validation now rejects them before writes; source/future derivative mapping and numeric zero targets have explicit coverage.
- Regeneration, current evidence, configuration, stale suggestion reuse and concurrent retries needed stronger semantics. Refreshes remain pending; approval/freeze revalidate current evidence and baseline; retries preserve actor identity and commit once.
- Audit/repository verification previously allowed inconsistent candidates or malformed ledger inputs and did not protect every materialized copy/index. Append-only candidate validation and graph-copy verification now fail corruption rather than repairing history silently.
- Unknown customer subcomponents discarded known information; invalid counts could hide behind a missing partner; whitespace scopes and malformed source references misrepresented reach. Known subcomponents retain documented bounds and malformed input shapes/counts/references fail validation.
- ECI accepted malformed traceability/concentration inputs. Explicit support IDs, region coverage, review collections and concentration counts are validated; opposing evidence does not add corroboration automatically.
- CSV had BMW headers whose values were blank for real backend field names. Actual contract aliases now populate those fields, and real DTO roundtrips verify preservation.
- Review/job/source/runtime edges lacked guard coverage: malformed citations/patches, orphan threads, stale model bases, progress failures, partial adapters, oversized generators, source path escape, driver ownership and unavailable dependencies now have acceptance cases.
- Freeze accepted incomplete opposing/context evidence snapshots. Every evidence relation now requires an exact pinned source version/locator and nonempty raw payload; rejected freezes leave state unchanged.
- Malformed source-provider responses and legacy status objects could produce 500 errors. Invalid adapter shapes/nonfinite metadata now return 503 and invalid transitions return 422. Admission persistence faults release locks and allow a later retry.
- Materialized revision native IDs, revision numbers and ownership relationships were not verified. Real graph tampering tests now establish that reads and writes fail closed, without silently restoring altered lineage.

## Observed runtime and limits

Real graph acceptance uses an isolated **Homebrew Neo4j 2026.09 with Java 21**, not the Compose image. Tests inspect rollback, exact persistence, concurrency, ledger/checkpoint tampering and materialized copies. The separate `graph_restart_probe.py` records exact state across an actual server STOP/START; driver reconnection alone is weaker evidence. Actual API lifespan and HTTP checks are distinct from source import success.

The **Neo4j 5.20 Compose image is untested** because Docker is unavailable. Role 4's UI is unavailable; configuration parsing does not establish UI→API networking. Actual Role 1/2 adapters, original-source reconciliation, live model generation and full raw-data conversion are absent. Those are sprint integration blockers, not passing backend tests.

All fixtures used for review are synthetic. Credentials, original feedback, extracted documents, private exports and database files must stay outside committed review artifacts.

Separately, the original baseline's private 250-record `requirements_full.json` passed the explicit legacy migration dry-run. Its summary reported 250 **unverified** records. This verifies artifact compatibility, not source reconciliation, PM approval or live migration. No original artifact contents are included here.

## Fresh review: correctness and unnecessary work

A fresh three-agent review and parent verification found additional defects after the earlier 675-test run. All findings below were reproduced and corrected; earlier passing totals were not treated as sign-off.

| Priority | Problem found | Correction and acceptance proof |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P0 | Engine-supplied resolved/accepted assumptions bypassed human acceptance. | Engine-origin target/assumption review states start pending; explicit PM resolution remains supported. `test_fresh_governance_review.py`. |
| P1 | Each small mutation rematerialized unrelated requirements and every historical snapshot. | Only changed current/mutable records and newly appended immutable records are materialized. Real graph recorder proves identical retries make zero materialization writes and changed progress writes only its job and ledger. `test_repository_review.py`. |
| P1 | Python equality allowed boolean/integer/float payload substitutions to appear unchanged. | Canonical JSON comparisons protect exact immutable values/types and detect mutable changes; graph tampering and rollback cases pass. |
| P1 | Deleting committed turns/runs/threads left orphan materialized graph copies. | Deletion is rejected before commit; tests verify unchanged state. |
| P1 | Multiple reads in one API response could combine different revisions, rankings or history. | Detail/history/thread/preview/dashboard/freeze-audit use one governance snapshot each. `test_fresh_api_review.py`. |
| P1 | Failed convenience challenge admission left an orphan thread. | Thread, challenge run and requested event admit together in one transaction; injected audit failure leaves none. |
| P1 | Import results accepted malformed/versionless snapshots; nonfinite metadata contaminated even the failed run. | Complete results pass finite JSON validation before run assignment; IDs, source versions, signal revisions and duplicate identities are checked. Rejection persists a clean failed run with no provenance events and permits the next job. |
| P1 | Duplicate shared-line forecasts dropped a source reference and depended on iteration order. | Shared volume counts once, every distinct reference survives in deterministic order, and outputs copy caller metadata. `test_fresh_scoring_review.py`. |
| P1 | Accepted near-unity weights could put priority above 100; known-input score and range differed by a rounding step. | Normalize accepted weights, store actual policy weights, use consistent contribution arithmetic and bound the scale. One seeded property test exercises 1,000 mixed inputs, bounds and override independence. |
| P2 | Unchanged generation after human review created redundant suggestions/events. | Comparison separates human review state from proposed content; approved/rejected/postponed and PM-resolved unchanged reruns preserve the entire state. |
| P2 | String flags such as contradiction='false' created false warnings; whitespace-only scoring assumptions passed. | Explicit boolean flags and nonblank assumption descriptions are required. |
| P2 | Health advertised success despite unreadable persistence. | Repository failure returns 503; optional missing model adapters remain separately reported. |
| P2 | Markdown repeated complete requirement JSON before repeating it in the full manifest. | Human headings/descriptions plus one complete manifest preserve reconstructability with one machine-readable copy. `test_fresh_export_review.py`. |

### Redundancy assessment

AST examination of **254 test functions** found no identical bodies after ignoring function names and docstrings. This is an exact-duplication check, not proof that all behavioral overlap is useful. Manual review retained unit/API/real-graph overlap because it checks different boundaries: formula/domain correctness, request serialization, transactional isolation and actual rollback. Negative type partitions and the 25 state/action combinations protect separate contract cases. The 1,000 scoring probes run within one seeded test rather than inflating the case count.

Measured actual Neo4j transactions: identical generation retry or repeated progress uses **10 integrity queries and zero materialization writes**; changed progress uses **12 queries**, including only its changed job and ledger. An unrelated five-revision history remains unchanged. Tampering with unrelated history still blocks a no-op retry without repair. API responses avoid duplicate ledger reads. Full locked graph-copy verification, whole-ledger serialization and ranking snapshots for exact active revision baselines remain deliberate prototype integrity costs; scalability is not established.

## Final verification — fresh review, 2026-10-10

**790 tests passed with Neo4j configured; no skips or failures.** The offline repeat passed 752 tests and skipped the 38 explicitly opt-in graph cases. Source files were frozen during the final instrumented run.

Passing coverage and a finite test suite cannot establish every possible input combination.

# Backend handoff

Role 3's governance implementation has been reviewed against [its assignment](../roles/03_BACKEND_AND_GOVERNANCE.md), [the implementation plan](../IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md), and [the challenge specification](../CHALLENGE_SPECIFICATION.md). The backend supports validated drafts, guarded human decisions, immutable revisions, deterministic scoring, audited review applications, complete exports and reconstructable approved freezes. The acceptance matrix and corrective findings are in [BACKEND_REVIEW.md](BACKEND_REVIEW.md).

**Full sprint integration sign-off remains pending:** actual Role 1/2 adapters, source reconciliation, live generation, Docker deployment and Role 4's UI workflow have not been demonstrated. Synthetic tests establish backend behavior; they do not establish the validity of original BMW evidence.

## Entry points and contracts

Run `services.api:app`; `pipeline/07_pm_review_api.py` delegates to the same application. [BACKEND_RUNTIME.md](BACKEND_RUNTIME.md) documents startup and the tested runtime boundary. [OpenAPI](../contracts/openapi.json) and [the synthetic fixture](../contracts/fixture_case.json) describe the HTTP contract. Shared models include source/evidence, signal/draft, review, score, revision, audit and freeze contracts. Preserve original legacy payloads through the explicit import/reconciliation path; do not relabel legacy 0–10 scores as v1.

`GET /api/requirements` returns `{items,total,offset,ranking_id}` and caps each page at 200. Complete CSV/JSON export uses `/api/requirements/export`, independently of pagination. CSV maps actual backend names such as `finding_links` and `evidence_links` into the required BMW columns while preserving original fields. Detail, evidence, history, history download, sources/records/pages, signal/thread review, run status, preview and freeze endpoints are provided. `API_PREFIX` changes the new-contract prefix; root aliases preserve selected legacy URLs, not every historical schema.

Every edit/decision/application requires an expected revision, named PM actor and nonblank rationale. Body and route IDs must match. Invalid domain inputs return 422, stale revisions/baselines 409, missing entities 404 and unavailable dependencies 503. Patches cannot change server-owned status, calculated scores or revisions. Edits/applications produce `PM_REVIEW` and clear approval and old overrides; application never grants approval. Approval requires human source, target/milestone and assumption confirmations, current verified evidence and cited strategic assessment. The named PM mechanism is a prototype identity input, not enterprise authentication.

Freeze rechecks selected approved revisions and evidence, captures complete requirement/source/configuration/ranking/decision payloads, and includes the full audit prefix through its retained checkpoint. Missing reconstructable source snapshots block freeze. Engine-supplied assumption/target review states start pending; only explicit human review can establish acceptance/resolution. Later edits leave committed snapshots unchanged. The hash chain is tamper-evident relative to a retained checkpoint; checkpoint retention outside the database remains an operational responsibility.

## Adapter responsibilities

`create_app` accepts injected `evidence_provider`, `source_provider`, `engine`, `import_service`, driver and repository. `BACKEND_ADAPTER_FACTORY=module:function` loads a synchronous factory during lifespan, passing `driver` and `repository`; it returns a mapping of those four adapter components. Invalid factories fail startup rather than silently replacing integrations.

- Evidence: `resolve(draft)` returns verified/traceable flags, authoritative `score_context`, `evidence_context`, pinned `source_snapshots`, and `required_assumption_ids`. Counts must describe the actual issue/cohort, forecasts need sourced 2030 locators, and fixed normalization is stored in immutable baseline configuration. Required successor/powertrain proxy IDs must identify the specific assumptions the PM must accept. Generic unrelated assumptions do not satisfy that guard. Native studies require reviewed relevant mappings; opaque channel labels remain opaque.
- Generation/review: `analyze(scope)` produces validated drafts with stable semantic identity; `review(entity, question, prior_turns)` returns cited answers, visible tool records and optional allowed patches. Review citations must resolve to authoritative source references. Signal review uses the same injected engine boundary. Model calls run outside governance transactions.
- Import: `import_data(scope)` returns validated import results and provenance snapshots. Import/consolidation provenance is audited when the adapter supplies it. Source-provider reads and graph-reference verification have synthetic and isolated graph acceptance, but Role 1's actual graph schema still needs reconciliation.
- Progress: adapters may accept `progress_callback`; supplied stage/progress/cache-mode updates are validated. Background jobs support partial results, bounded analysis batches, shared admission and same-thread review serialization. Interrupted jobs recover truthfully as failed. Execution is in-process, not a durable distributed queue.

The default runtime has no production evidence/generation/import implementation. A configured provider key alone does not install one. Source queries assume the documented graph schema; an empty result is not proof that BMW sources were imported.

## Remaining acceptance

1. Connect actual Role 1 evidence/import/source adapters and reconcile original feedback IDs, native study mappings, strategy passages, source snapshots and sourced 2030 forecasts. Preserve private data outside public commits.
2. Connect Role 2 generation/review, verify stable reruns and rejected/approved preservation with real source lineage, cited answers and visible tool records. Demonstrate live provider use and any cache behavior honestly.

### Redundancy assessment

AST examination of **254 test functions** found no identical bodies after ignoring function names and docstrings. This is an exact-duplication check, not proof that all behavioral overlap is useful. Manual review retained unit/API/real-graph overlap because it checks different boundaries: formula/domain correctness, request serialization, transactional isolation and actual rollback. Negative type partitions and the 25 state/action combinations protect separate contract cases. The 1,000 scoring probes run within one seeded test rather than inflating the case count.

Measured actual Neo4j transactions: identical generation retry or repeated progress uses **10 integrity queries and zero materialization writes**; changed progress uses **12 queries**, including only its changed job and ledger. An unrelated five-revision history remains unchanged. Tampering with unrelated history still blocks a no-op retry without repair. API responses avoid duplicate ledger reads. Full locked graph-copy verification, whole-ledger serialization and ranking snapshots for exact active revision baselines remain deliberate prototype integrity costs; scalability is not established.

## Adapter responsibilities

Required successor/powertrain proxy IDs must identify the specific assumptions the PM must accept. Generic unrelated assumptions do not satisfy that guard. Native studies require reviewed relevant mappings; opaque channel labels remain opaque.

Review citations must resolve to authoritative source references. Signal review uses the same injected engine boundary. Model calls run outside governance transactions.
- Import: `import_data(scope)` returns validated import results and provenance snapshots. Import/consolidation provenance is audited when the adapter supplies it. Source-provider reads and graph-reference verification have synthetic and isolated graph acceptance, but Role 1's actual graph schema still needs reconciliation.
- Progress: adapters may accept `progress_callback`; supplied stage/progress/cache-mode updates are validated. Background jobs support partial results, bounded analysis batches, shared admission and same-thread review serialization. Interrupted jobs recover truthfully as failed. Execution is in-process, not a durable distributed queue.

Supply `BACKEND_TEST_NEO4J_URI` and, if necessary, `BACKEND_TEST_NEO4J_USER`, `BACKEND_TEST_NEO4J_PASSWORD`, `BACKEND_TEST_NEO4J_DATABASE` through the environment, then run the same suite. Tests create random backend namespaces and remove only their own nodes; uniqueness constraints remain. An absent graph URI skips opt-in tests; a configured but inaccessible graph fails.

Observed graph verification used existing **Homebrew Neo4j 2026.09 and Java 21**, with an isolated database under `/private/tmp/bmw-backend-neo4j` and Bolt port 17687. Tests inspect transaction rollback after audit/materialization failures, concurrent mutations, state persistence, retained-checkpoint ledger tampering, immutable materialized copies/indexes and API lifespan/HTTP behavior. A separately recorded `tests/backend/graph_restart_probe.py prepare`/`verify` check spans an actual server STOP/START and checks exact saved state. Treat it separately from driver reconnect tests.

Provider checks cover OpenAI-only, Anthropic-only, automatic/explicit selection and missing/whitespace keys. Runner configuration and shell syntax have been exercised using synthetic configuration. `requirements.txt` pins direct dependencies; `requirements.lock.txt` records the complete installed Python 3.12 environment, including transitive versions. The lock was captured on macOS; clean installation and container/platform compatibility remain to be verified. The Dockerfile applies the recorded versions as constraints.

Regenerate public contracts using `PYTHONPATH=.:tests/backend .venv/bin/python tests/backend/generate_contracts.py`. Examples come from actual synthetic API calls and retain verifiable audit timestamps/hashes. Contract acceptance validates the models, scoring, checkpoint and exported OpenAPI against the current application.

No successful live model call, original BMW raw-conversion run or actual UI workflow has been demonstrated. Missing source/model adapters and unavailable Docker/UI remain integration blockers. An empty source/export response or passing health endpoint establishes startup/query behavior, not an imported source-to-approved-plan workflow.

# BMW Product Management Challenge: Assignment Specification & Requirements Guide

**Challenge:** AI for Product Decision Making  
**Host:** BMW Group Product Management  
**Scope Focus:** Automotive Product Development Process — Steps 1 & 2 (Market Research & Product Planning to Gate G1 Concept Freeze)  
**Target Derivatives:** BMW 1 Series (F70), BMW 5 Series (G60/G68), BMW 7 Series (G70), and Future Successor Lines (Neue Klasse Architecture)  
**Target Markets:** Europe (EU), United States (US), China (CN), and Rest of World (RoW)  

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Mission Statement

Modern automotive product management requires synthesizing billions of fragmented market signals, customer reviews, warranty reports, competitor actions, and strategic corporate roadmaps into a coherent, customer-facing product specification. Today, this process spans approximately **two years** per vehicle generation and is predominantly manual, fragmented, and vulnerable to subjective bias.

### The Mission
Develop an AI-powered, human-in-the-loop enterprise application that:
1. **Ingests Heterogeneous Data**: Combines internal BMW customer feedback, quantitative satisfaction surveys, vehicle equipment catalogs, and strategic corporate reports.
2. **Extracts Actionable Signals**: Discovers recurring complaints, unmet customer needs, competitor advantages, and emerging market trends, each strictly linked to originating evidence.
3. **Derives SMART Product Requirements**: Formulates clear, customer-facing, realistic, and measurable requirements adhering to SMART criteria.
4. **Prioritizes with Explainable Logic**: Applies an objective, transparent, multi-factor scoring methodology that balances customer value, regional volume impact, corporate strategy, and implementation complexity.
5. **Keeps the Product Manager Firmly in the Loop**: Enables the PM to review, approve, reject, modify, or challenge requirements, rationales, and underlying evidence.
6. **Maintains a Forensic Audit Trail**: Chronologically logs every system derivation, PM intervention, score override, and decision rationale to guarantee end-to-end governance.

---

## 2. Automotive Product Development Process Alignment

BMW management explicitly bounded the scope of this challenge to **Steps 1 and 2** of the 13-stage Automotive Product Development Lifecycle:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Step1["Step 1: Market Research & Needs Analysis"]
        A1["Activities: Market Research, Customer Insights, Competitor Benchmarking, Trend Analysis"]
        A2["Deliverables: Market Opportunity Report, Customer Needs Document, Target Segments"]
        G0["Decision Gate: G0 — Project Approval"]
        A1 --> A2 --> G0
    end

    subgraph Step2["Step 2: Product Planning (Core App Focus)"]
        B1["Activities: Define Product Vision, Positioning, SMART Feature Prioritization, Trade-off Resolution"]
        B2["Deliverables: Product Plan, Project Charter, Prioritized Requirement List, Initial Business Sizing"]
        G1["Decision Gate: G1 — Concept Freeze"]
        B1 --> B2 --> G1
    end

    subgraph Step3["Steps 3 to 13: Concept to Continuous Feedback"]
        C1["G2 Feasibility -> G3 Design Freeze -> ... -> G9 SOP -> Step 13 Market Feedback Loop"]
    end

    Step1 --> Step2 --> Step3

    classDef default fill:#ffffff,stroke:#000000,color:#000000,stroke-width:1px;
    style Step1 fill:#ffffff,stroke:#000000,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#000000
    style Step2 fill:#ffffff,stroke:#000000,stroke-width:2px,color:#000000
    style Step3 fill:#ffffff,stroke:#000000,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#000000
```

### Boundary Definitions
* **In-Scope (Customer-Facing Product Attributes)**:
  * Interior comfort, ergonomics, and spatial packaging
  * Infotainment, operating system UX, and connected digital services
  * Climatization and thermal comfort controls
  * Driving experience and dynamic perception
  * Real-world charging UX and range perception
  * Equipment packaging, option bundling, and regional variant differentiation
* **Out-of-Scope**:
  * Regulatory and homologation compliance (e.g., UNECE safety, emissions type approval)
  * Low-level component specifications and supplier engineering schematics
  * Detailed unit economics, factory tooling capex, and bill-of-materials pricing calculations (rough implementation complexity/effort sizing is utilized as a prioritization factor)

---

## 3. Data Ecosystem & Inputs Profile

The application processes four distinct tiers of heterogeneous data:

```
BMW-Data/
├── F70_feedback_hackathon.xlsx              # 4,076 rows (1 Series - UK, JP, SE, FR)
├── G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx              # 5,005 rows (5 Series - US, KR, GB, JP, SE)
├── G70_feedback_hackathon.xlsx              # 4,690 rows (7 Series - US, KR, JP, GB, CA)
├── F70_G60_G68_G70_customer_studies.xlsx    # Quantitative satisfaction studies (China, EU, US)
├── sales_volumes.xlsx                       # Market deliveries (2024, 2025, 2030 projections)
├── F70_OptionList.PDF                       # Official German equipment catalog & packaging (1er)
├── G60_OptionList.PDF                       # Official German equipment catalog & packaging (5er)
├── G70_OptionList.PDF                       # Official German equipment catalog & packaging (7er)
└── BMW_Group_Report_2025.pdf / Q-Deck       # 400-page strategic corporate & financial report
```

### Dataset Characteristics

| Dataset | Volume | Key Attributes | Strategic Value |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Customer Feedback** | 13,771 rows | `ID`, `Country`, `Engine Type` (ICE, BEV, PHEV), `Feedback Type` (Likes, DTU, Defect, Wants), `Customer Feedback`, `Vfc Category` | Voice of the customer; ground-truth operational friction, ergonomics, and feature desires. |
| **Customer Studies** | Quantitative sheets | Likert ratings (US) & Mean satisfaction scores (CN vs. EU) across 15 vehicle systems | Macro-level customer satisfaction benchmarks; correlates qualitative text with quantitative validation. |
| **Sales Volumes** | 4 regions $\times$ 3 vehicle lines | Volumes for 2024, 2025, and 2030 projections across EU, US, China, and RoW | Objective volume weighting factor for prioritization formulas. |
| **Option Catalogs** | 3 German PDFs | Standard vs. optional equipment, option codes, bundle packages (Innovation, Travel, Comfort) | Grounds proposed requirements in realistic production packaging. |
| **Strategic Report Deck** | ~400 pages | Neue Klasse platform roadmap, R&D priorities, BEV delivery targets, digital software KPIs | Strategic validation layer; ties customer desires to BMW engineering investments. |

---

## 4. Evaluation Criteria & Scoring Rubric

The challenge will be judged on five primary criteria, with one critical guiding principle:

| Dimension | Weight | Key Evaluation Requirements |
| :--- | :---: | :--- |
| **Decision & Scoring Logic** | 25% | Quality, consistency, and mathematical explainability of prioritization. Clear demonstration of how evidence sources are weighted and combined, and how trade-offs and conflicting signals are resolved. |
| **Workflow & Human Decision-Making** | 20% | Completeness of the end-to-end workflow from raw findings to prioritized requirements. Clearly defined roles, decision gates, and boundaries between autonomous AI and mandatory human review. |
| **Traceability & Auditability** | 20% | Full backward lineage from every requirement and score back to originating quotes, surveys, and report slides. Complete, chronological, tamper-evident audit history of all approvals, edits, and rejections. |
| **Solution Quality, Usability & Feasibility** | 20% | Prototype UI/UX polish, usability for BMW Product Managers and engineering peers, realistic applicability in an enterprise automotive environment, and quality of SMART formulations. |
| **Innovation, Scalability & Business Impact** | 15% | Originality of approach, cross-derivative scalability (F70 $\to$ G60 $\to$ G70 $\to$ Neue Klasse), reduction in manual requirement definition cycle time, and prevention of costly late-stage engineering rework. |

### The Winning Differentiator: "We Reward Honesty"
> **Direct Quote from BMW Challenge Evaluation Criteria:**  
> *"We reward honesty. Trustworthy AI acknowledges uncertainty. Show us where your app lacks evidence, encounters conflicting signals, or reaches uncertain conclusions, and how this is surfaced to the PM. Honest limitations are a strength, not a weakness."*

The application must include an explicit **Uncertainty & Evidence Confidence Index** that transparently highlights:
1. Low sample size / weak empirical support
2. Regional contradictions (e.g., EU Autobahn driver desires vs. China chauffeur comfort)
3. Extrapolations based on forward-looking assumptions (e.g., 2030 battery/software tech) versus proven historical data

---

## 5. SMART Requirements Framework

BMW requirements must strictly comply with the **SMART** standard:

| SMART Dimension | Definition | Automotive Context |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Specific** | Concrete and unambiguous system or feature scope | Exact UI component, sensor, or interior system |
| **Measurable** | Objective engineering/UX KPIs & thresholds | Clear quantifiable metrics (e.g. latency $< 45\text{ms}$, 60 fps) |
| **Attainable** | Feasible within vehicle architecture & manufacturing | Compatible with platform packaging & wiring harness |
| **Relevant** | Meaningfully solves verified customer pain | Directly resolves top complaint or aligns with brand strategy |
| **Timely** | Explicit SOP target & vehicle milestone | SOP 2028 (LCI / Successor / Neue Klasse milestone) |

### Benchmark Example: From Complaint to SMART Requirement
* **Raw Voice of Customer (`G70-0891`)**: *"Customer noted she would have chosen the Home theater screen, but it obstructs the view out the rear and BMW does not offer a camera/rear-view mirror screen."*
* **Unacceptable Requirement (Vague)**: *"Improve rear visibility when the theater screen is down."*
* **SMART Requirement (`REQ-G70-VIS-001`)**:
  * **Specific**: Full-display digital streaming rear-view mirror system utilizing an aerodynamic roof-mounted wide-angle camera feeding directly into the central rear-view mirror.
  * **Measurable**: End-to-end video latency $< 45\text{ ms}$; frame rate $\ge 60\text{ fps}$ at $1080\text{p}$; dynamic range $> 120\text{ dB}$ (headlight anti-glare); camera lens auto-defrosting and wash nozzle operational from $-30^\circ\text{C}$ to $+65^\circ\text{C}$.
  * **Attainable**: Integrates with the existing Neue Klasse roof shark-fin camera housing and high-speed automotive Ethernet backbone.
  * **Relevant**: Eliminates the #1 safety blocker preventing theater screen adoption; projected to increase Theater Screen package take-rate by 18%.
  * **Timely**: Targeted for SOP 2028 (G70 LCI / Neue Klasse Luxury derivative).
  * **Package Strategy**: Standard on i7 M70; optional in Innovation Package for base derivatives.

---

## 6. Key Mentors & Stakeholder Insights

1. **Bene_BMW (Product Management Pain Points)**:
   * *Cross-Market Regional Balancing*: Preferences differ radically by climate, usage habits, and culture. A single global specification often fails in either Europe, the US, or China.
   * *Predecessor Feedback Cycles*: Capturing field insights from outgoing models (e.g., F70, G60, G70) and projecting them 3–5 years ahead into future vehicle architectures.
   * *2-Year Timeline*: Requirement prioritization is not a one-time script; it is a collaborative, iterative governance process over ~24 months.
2. **ThomasFremuthBMW**:
   * Ground proposals in real evidence; maintain strict data hygiene (do not commit raw internal data to public repositories).
3. **Sebastian_BMW & ThomasBMW**:
   * Scope is tightly focused on Steps 1 & 2 of the automotive development framework.

---

## 7. Expected Deliverables

### 7.1 BMW-Provided Deliverable Wording

The following four expected deliverables are reproduced from the BMW wording supplied to the team.

#### 1. Concept and Demonstrable Prototype

> A concept and demonstrable prototype of an AI-powered product requirements application that processes heterogeneous inputs, derives product requirements, supports prioritization, and integrates human review.

#### 2. Structured Sample Requirements List

> A structured sample list of derived product requirements. Each requirement should include a unique identifier, a clear and actionable description, its linked findings and sources, a priority or score, the applied prioritization rationale, an evidence level, the key future-facing assumptions and uncertainties and its current decision status.

#### 3. End-to-End Workflow

> A clearly defined end-to-end workflow showing how inputs are processed into proposed and prioritized requirements, which activities the AI performs autonomously, and where human review is mandatory.

#### 4. Demonstrable Audit Trail

> A demonstrable audit trail that makes each requirement traceable from its underlying findings and sources through consolidation, scoring, prioritization, and human decision-making. It should record relevant changes to requirement content, scores, priorities, evidence, and status, including who or what initiated each change, when it occurred, and the documented rationale.

### 7.2 Delivery Checklist

- [ ] **Concept & Working Application Prototype**: Explain the concept and demonstrate heterogeneous input processing, derived product requirements, prioritization, and integrated human review.
- [ ] **Structured Sample Requirements List**: Include a unique identifier, clear and actionable description, linked findings and sources, priority or score, applied prioritization rationale, evidence level, key future-facing assumptions and uncertainties, and current decision status for every requirement.
- [ ] **End-to-End Workflow Definition**: Show how inputs become proposed and prioritized requirements, which activities the AI performs autonomously, and where human review is mandatory.
- [ ] **Traceable & Reconstructable Audit Trail**: Trace requirements from findings and sources through consolidation, scoring, prioritization, and human decisions. Record relevant content, score, priority, evidence, and status changes with initiator, timestamp, and rationale.

### 7.3 Presentation Deliverable

- [ ] **Pitch Presentation Deck (3–5 min)**: Compelling narrative demonstrating real-world value, data grounding, and Trustworthy AI principles.

See `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` for the concrete prototype features, artifact formats, implementation responsibilities, and acceptance criteria mapped to these deliverables.

## Interfaces and Handoffs

```python
search_feedback(query, scope, limit=20)
get_source_record(record_id)
get_survey_facts(topic, scope)
get_sales_facts(scope, year=2030)
search_document_chunks(query, scope, document_kind=None, limit=6)
get_comment_cohort_counts(scope)
```

Each result includes stable ID, source-file hash/version, original text/value, locator, source/target applicability metadata, and explicit unknowns. Workbook locators contain sheet/row/column; PDFs use 1-based physical page and optional printed page label. Preserve original and normalized powertrain/category values.

Role 2 calls these functions for extraction/retrieval. Role 3 wraps them in HTTP endpoints and uses them for scoring/validation. Role 4 consumes those endpoints, not your database code.

Use injected driver/transaction and an audit sink. Evidence imports record events within their transaction; the sink never commits independently. Independent tests can use fake repositories/sinks before a live Neo4j integration.

## Implementation Details
### 5.4 Draft Validation and Persistence

Pydantic validates the output shape. Service validation checks:

1. Each output includes its requested input group/signal ID and cites supplied immutable evidence/source versions; map by input ID rather than array position. Unknown/duplicate IDs fail validation; missing outputs create explicit partial results.
2. Quoted spans are exact; fact values match the stored facts.
3. Supporting customer evidence exists for the problem statement, or the draft explicitly identifies a study-only basis.
4. Markets, powertrains, source derivatives, and target derivatives are explicit.
5. A narrow requirement does not claim the full topic count as support.
6. Unsupported quantitative claims and future assumptions are labeled.
7. Regulatory engineering and detailed component/BOM specifications do not replace the customer-facing requirement.

Use collision-resistant full-scope signal/derivation IDs rather than VFC prefixes or per-run ordinals. Persist new signal/requirement revisions without overwriting human decisions. Generation can include a traceable weak-evidence draft with explicit limitations; the legacy STRONG/MODERATE-only filter must not hide the uncertainty demonstration.

Citation/number checks establish traceability, not semantic proof that a passage entails the claim. The draft records its interpretation for PM review.

Then the backend assigns a stable unique requirement/derivation ID, calculates scores and evidence quality, saves revision 1 with status `DRAFT`, records the derivation, and refreshes the baseline ranking. Invalid drafts are retained as run failures for inspection but do not appear as valid proposed requirements. Drafting belongs to Owner 2; persistence/scoring belongs to Owner 3.

Implementation sequence inside `analysis.py`:

```python
async def derive_one(signal, scope, run_id):
    pack = retrieval.build_evidence_pack(signal, scope)
    draft = await llm.draft_requirement(signal, pack, scope)
    validated = validate_draft(draft, pack, signal)
    scores = scoring.calculate(validated, signal, baseline_config)
    evidence = scoring.assess_evidence(validated, signal, pack)
    # Backend writer uses one managed Neo4j transaction for revision/rank/audit.
    # All network/model calls above complete before that transaction starts.
    return requirement_writer.create_draft(validated, scores, evidence, run_id)
```

This shows the path for a new requirement; the service checks cached/existing derivations before entering it. Imports, model calls, and evidence retrieval remain independently callable/testable modules.

### 5.5 Run Behavior and Failure Handling

Run stages: `import_check → consolidate → retrieve → draft → validate → score → completed`.

Run states: `queued`, `running`, `succeeded`, `partial`, `failed`. Return a run ID immediately, show progress, and poll while running. Execute one generation run at a time in the first build.

- Cache by source/config versions, signal revision, scope, model, prompt version, and retrieved-context hash.
- Cached derivations return existing requirement IDs without duplicating or overwriting them. Regenerating an existing requirement produces a pending suggestion/diff for PM application, preserving the current revision and decision.
- Use a bounded concurrency limit and at most one structured-output repair attempt per draft; transient provider errors receive bounded backoff.
- Save valid requirements even if another signal fails, and report partial results.
- On restart, mark interrupted runs `failed` with reason `interrupted`, rather than leaving them permanently running.
- Missing credentials or unavailable providers produce a visible failure/configuration state. Cached results are labeled cached; no fabricated successful AI run.

### 5.6 Tool-Enabled Review Assistant

Expose typed function tools through `tool_registry.py`; the server dispatches them to existing services. Tools return structured identifiers, source locations, exact text/facts, counts, and explicit missing-data results.

| Tool | Inputs | Output / service |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `search_feedback` | Query, derivative/region/powertrain scope, limit | Original comments, matching spans, source references, and candidate/membership distinction |
| `get_signal_evidence` | Signal ID/revision | Supporting/opposing evidence, distinct counts, assignment coverage, and gaps |
| `get_survey_facts` | Topic and scope | Native study values/distributions, cells, mapping strength, unknown sample/scale metadata |
| `get_sales_volume` | Vehicle lines, regions, forecast year | Deterministic applicable volume, fact references, missing splits, proxy assumptions |
| `search_documents` | Query, document kind, derivative/market scope, limit | Equipment/strategy chunks with exact text and PDF page references |
| `get_requirement_context` | Requirement ID/revision | Current reviewed content, scores, assumptions, evidence, and selected history |
| `preview_requirement_change` | Requirement ID/expected revision and allowed field patch | Validated hypothetical content, recalculated score/ECI/rank effects, and unresolved checks; no writes |

The review service loads the selected entity and current revision before a model turn. It sends the PM question, relevant prior visible conversation, pinned context, and tool schemas. The model can request tools, receive results, and produce an answer or pending suggestion.

Implementation limits:

- At most six tool invocations and four model round-trips per turn, including repair attempts; bounded result sizes. Return a partial answer with its limitation if the budget is exhausted.
- Server validates tool arguments and uses parameterized queries and registered source IDs. Tools cannot execute arbitrary SQL, access arbitrary files, or modify requirements.
- Record tool inputs/results and their source versions with the turn/run so the answer is reconstructable.
- Feedback/documents are evidence content, not instructions for the assistant. Only the registered tool schemas and service policy determine execution.
- The model can propose edits to title/description, SMART fields, target scope, assumptions, evidence links, and scoring-factor assessments. It cannot patch source text, calculated scores, status, actor, revision number, or audit history.
- Every suggested patch is validated and previewed by the backend, even if the model did not call the preview tool itself. New evidence must resolve to real stored identifiers.

Final review result: cited `answer`, `coverage_gaps`, optional `proposed_patch`, server-calculated `score_preview`, `base_revision`, and proposal state (`none`, `pending`, `applied`, `discarded`, `stale`). Persist it before displaying it. Model failure does not prevent ordinary form-based PM edits.

### 9.1 API Endpoints

Register the static `/api/requirements/export` route before the `/{id}` route. Run polling uses a common response shape for import, analysis, and challenge jobs.

All contextual chat uses the same review service. The convenience challenge route is an adapter, not a second implementation. Applying a proposal is idempotent by turn ID; an identical repeat request returns the original application result rather than creating another revision. A conflicting reapplication returns 409. Record the application result and requirement mutation in the same transaction.

Example approval request:

```json

  "action": "approve",
  "expected_revision": 3,
  "actor_id": "pm-demo-1",
```

The server determines the new revision, status, timestamp, score, and events. The client cannot submit a fabricated approval state or final calculated score.

## Implementation Details
### 5.4 Draft Validation and Persistence

Pydantic validates the output shape. Service validation checks:

1. Each output includes its requested input group/signal ID and cites supplied immutable evidence/source versions; map by input ID rather than array position. Unknown/duplicate IDs fail validation; missing outputs create explicit partial results.
2. Quoted spans are exact; fact values match the stored facts.
3. Supporting customer evidence exists for the problem statement, or the draft explicitly identifies a study-only basis.
4. Markets, powertrains, source derivatives, and target derivatives are explicit.
5. A narrow requirement does not claim the full topic count as support.
6. Unsupported quantitative claims and future assumptions are labeled.
7. Regulatory engineering and detailed component/BOM specifications do not replace the customer-facing requirement.

Use collision-resistant full-scope signal/derivation IDs rather than VFC prefixes or per-run ordinals. Persist new signal/requirement revisions without overwriting human decisions. Generation can include a traceable weak-evidence draft with explicit limitations; the legacy STRONG/MODERATE-only filter must not hide the uncertainty demonstration.

Citation/number checks establish traceability, not semantic proof that a passage entails the claim. The draft records its interpretation for PM review.

Then the backend assigns a stable unique requirement/derivation ID, calculates scores and evidence quality, saves revision 1 with status `DRAFT`, records the derivation, and refreshes the baseline ranking. Invalid drafts are retained as run failures for inspection but do not appear as valid proposed requirements. Drafting belongs to Owner 2; persistence/scoring belongs to Owner 3.

Implementation sequence inside `analysis.py`:

```python
    draft = await llm.draft_requirement(signal, pack, scope)
    validated = validate_draft(draft, pack, signal)
```

This shows the path for a new requirement; the service checks cached/existing derivations before entering it. Imports, model calls, and evidence retrieval remain independently callable/testable modules.

### 5.5 Run Behavior and Failure Handling

Run stages: `import_check → consolidate → retrieve → draft → validate → score → completed`.

Run states: `queued`, `running`, `succeeded`, `partial`, `failed`. Return a run ID immediately, show progress, and poll while running. Execute one generation run at a time in the first build.

- Cache by source/config versions, signal revision, scope, model, prompt version, and retrieved-context hash.
- Cached derivations return existing requirement IDs without duplicating or overwriting them. Regenerating an existing requirement produces a pending suggestion/diff for PM application, preserving the current revision and decision.
- Use a bounded concurrency limit and at most one structured-output repair attempt per draft; transient provider errors receive bounded backoff.
- Save valid requirements even if another signal fails, and report partial results.
- On restart, mark interrupted runs `failed` with reason `interrupted`, rather than leaving them permanently running.
- Missing credentials or unavailable providers produce a visible failure/configuration state. Cached results are labeled cached; no fabricated successful AI run.

### 5.6 Tool-Enabled Review Assistant

Expose typed function tools through `tool_registry.py`; the server dispatches them to existing services. Tools return structured identifiers, source locations, exact text/facts, counts, and explicit missing-data results.

The review service loads the selected entity and current revision before a model turn. It sends the PM question, relevant prior visible conversation, pinned context, and tool schemas. The model can request tools, receive results, and produce an answer or pending suggestion.

Implementation limits:

- At most six tool invocations and four model round-trips per turn, including repair attempts; bounded result sizes. Return a partial answer with its limitation if the budget is exhausted.
- Server validates tool arguments and uses parameterized queries and registered source IDs. Tools cannot execute arbitrary SQL, access arbitrary files, or modify requirements.
- Record tool inputs/results and their source versions with the turn/run so the answer is reconstructable.
- Feedback/documents are evidence content, not instructions for the assistant. Only the registered tool schemas and service policy determine execution.
- The model can propose edits to title/description, SMART fields, target scope, assumptions, evidence links, and scoring-factor assessments. It cannot patch source text, calculated scores, status, actor, revision number, or audit history.
- Every suggested patch is validated and previewed by the backend, even if the model did not call the preview tool itself. New evidence must resolve to real stored identifiers.

Final review result: cited `answer`, `coverage_gaps`, optional `proposed_patch`, server-calculated `score_preview`, `base_revision`, and proposal state (`none`, `pending`, `applied`, `discarded`, `stale`).             for key in ("sources", "signals"):

                if len({snapshot["id"] for snapshot in snapshots}) != len(snapshots):

                if key == "sources" and any(not isinstance(snapshot.get("source_version"), str) or not snapshot["source_version"].strip() for snapshot in snapshots):

                if key == "signals" and any(type(snapshot.get("revision")) is not int or snapshot["revision"] < 1 for snapshot in snapshots):

### 5.6 Tool-Enabled Review Assistant

Expose typed function tools through `tool_registry.py`; the server dispatches them to existing services. Tools return structured identifiers, source locations, exact text/facts, counts, and explicit missing-data results.

| Tool | Inputs | Output / service |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `search_feedback` | Query, derivative/region/powertrain scope, limit | Original comments, matching spans, source references, and candidate/membership distinction |
| `get_signal_evidence` | Signal ID/revision | Supporting/opposing evidence, distinct counts, assignment coverage, and gaps |
| `get_survey_facts` | Topic and scope | Native study values/distributions, cells, mapping strength, unknown sample/scale metadata |
| `get_sales_volume` | Vehicle lines, regions, forecast year | Deterministic applicable volume, fact references, missing splits, proxy assumptions |
| `search_documents` | Query, document kind, derivative/market scope, limit | Equipment/strategy chunks with exact text and PDF page references |
| `get_requirement_context` | Requirement ID/revision | Current reviewed content, scores, assumptions, evidence, and selected history |
| `preview_requirement_change` | Requirement ID/expected revision and allowed field patch | Validated hypothetical content, recalculated score/ECI/rank effects, and unresolved checks; no writes |

The review service loads the selected entity and current revision before a model turn. It sends the PM question, relevant prior visible conversation, pinned context, and tool schemas. The model can request tools, receive results, and produce an answer or pending suggestion.

Implementation limits:

- At most six tool invocations and four model round-trips per turn, including repair attempts; bounded result sizes. Return a partial answer with its limitation if the budget is exhausted.
- Server validates tool arguments and uses parameterized queries and registered source IDs. Tools cannot execute arbitrary SQL, access arbitrary files, or modify requirements.
- Record tool inputs/results and their source versions with the turn/run so the answer is reconstructable.
- Feedback/documents are evidence content, not instructions for the assistant. Only the registered tool schemas and service policy determine execution.
- The model can propose edits to title/description, SMART fields, target scope, assumptions, evidence links, and scoring-factor assessments. It cannot patch source text, calculated scores, status, actor, revision number, or audit history.
- Every suggested patch is validated and previewed by the backend, even if the model did not call the preview tool itself. New evidence must resolve to real stored identifiers.

Final review result: cited `answer`, `coverage_gaps`, optional `proposed_patch`, server-calculated `score_preview`, `base_revision`, and proposal state (`none`, `pending`, `applied`, `discarded`, `stale`). Persist it before displaying it. Model failure does not prevent ordinary form-based PM edits.

### 5.6 Tool-Enabled Review Assistant

Expose typed function tools through `tool_registry.py`; the server dispatches them to existing services. Tools return structured identifiers, source locations, exact text/facts, counts, and explicit missing-data results.

| Tool | Inputs | Output / service |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `search_feedback` | Query, derivative/region/powertrain scope, limit | Original comments, matching spans, source references, and candidate/membership distinction |
| `get_signal_evidence` | Signal ID/revision | Supporting/opposing evidence, distinct counts, assignment coverage, and gaps |
| `get_survey_facts` | Topic and scope | Native study values/distributions, cells, mapping strength, unknown sample/scale metadata |
| `get_sales_volume` | Vehicle lines, regions, forecast year | Deterministic applicable volume, fact references, missing splits, proxy assumptions |
| `search_documents` | Query, document kind, derivative/market scope, limit | Equipment/strategy chunks with exact text and PDF page references |
| `get_requirement_context` | Requirement ID/revision | Current reviewed content, scores, assumptions, evidence, and selected history |
| `preview_requirement_change` | Requirement ID/expected revision and allowed field patch | Validated hypothetical content, recalculated score/ECI/rank effects, and unresolved checks; no writes |

The review service loads the selected entity and current revision before a model turn. It sends the PM question, relevant prior visible conversation, pinned context, and tool schemas. The model can request tools, receive results, and produce an answer or pending suggestion.

Implementation limits:

- At most six tool invocations and four model round-trips per turn, including repair attempts; bounded result sizes. Return a partial answer with its limitation if the budget is exhausted.
- Server validates tool arguments and uses parameterized queries and registered source IDs. Tools cannot execute arbitrary SQL, access arbitrary files, or modify requirements.
- Record tool inputs/results and their source versions with the turn/run so the answer is reconstructable.
- Feedback/documents are evidence content, not instructions for the assistant. Only the registered tool schemas and service policy determine execution.
- The model can propose edits to title/description, SMART fields, target scope, assumptions, evidence links, and scoring-factor assessments. It cannot patch source text, calculated scores, status, actor, revision number, or audit history.
- Every suggested patch is validated and previewed by the backend, even if the model did not call the preview tool itself. New evidence must resolve to real stored identifiers.

Final review result: cited `answer`, `coverage_gaps`, optional `proposed_patch`, server-calculated `score_preview`, `base_revision`, and proposal state (`none`, `pending`, `applied`, `discarded`, `stale`). Persist it before displaying it. Model failure does not prevent ordinary form-based PM edits.

## 6. The Requirement Contract

**Role 03 stays within its ownership scope, but I would not sign off full compliance yet.** I read `/docs`, the role assignments, implementation plan and challenge specification, then inspected the code and reran the backend suite.

**Validation:** 752 tests passed; 38 real-Neo4j tests were skipped. The docs report an earlier 790-test graph-enabled run; I did not independently repeat that run.

The main findings are:

- **Review results lose required information.** [services/api.py:380](/Users/razvi/Desktop/BMWChallenge/services/api.py:380) saves a selected subset of the engine response. Dedicated coverage gaps and model/prompt metadata are not retained. The plan requires persisted gap information, and Role 02 requires model/prompt metadata for reconstructable review turns. The adapter contract needs explicit fields and backend persistence for them.

- **Suggestion preview is incomplete.** [services/api.py:379](/Users/razvi/Desktop/BMWChallenge/services/api.py:379) computes the priority score, but does not return recalculated ECI, rank effects or unresolved review checks. Those are expected by the plan’s change-preview contract and Role 04’s review workbench.

- **Role 01’s handoff needs further alignment.** The backend provides source/record/chunk endpoints and an injected evidence resolver, but does not wrap the feedback search, survey facts, sales facts, document search and cohort-count interfaces listed in [Role 01:54](/Users/razvi/Desktop/BMWChallenge/roles/01_DATA_AND_EVIDENCE.md:54). Also, the import adapter runs before the backend provenance transaction; the current interface does not establish the shared import/audit transaction required by Role 01. These remain integration contract gaps.

The ties otherwise look appropriate:

| Role | Assessment |
|---|---|
| **01 — Data/evidence** | Backend consumes authoritative evidence and pinned sources without implementing parsers. Actual schema, evidence resolution and import/audit integration remain pending. |
| **02 — AI/review** | Injected generation/review boundary, backend scoring, guarded application and preserved human decisions are appropriate. Actual engine integration remains pending, with the review-contract gaps above. |
| **04 — Frontend** | API endpoints, OpenAPI, synthetic fixtures, decision guards and `http://api:8000` configuration support the expected client. Actual UI and container networking remain unverified. |

**Scope check passed:** I found no production frontend, data parser or AI prompt implementation belonging to the other roles. Shared models, source adapters, synthetic fixtures and runtime configuration fit Role 03’s assigned responsibilities.

The governance core is well covered: human decision guards, immutable revisions, overrides, scoring/ECI, transactional audit, complete exports and freezes. However, passing backend tests does not establish the challenge’s real source-to-approved-package workflow. The docs correctly disclose the missing production adapters, reconciled BMW evidence, live generation, Docker and UI acceptance.

No implementation files were changed.

"""Role 03 review persistence and authoritative hypothetical changes."""
import copy
import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from conftest import FakeEvidence, fixture_draft
from test_review import FakeEngine, identity, create_thread, ask
from test_fresh_api_review import ProbeRepository
from services.api import create_app
from services.repository import MemoryRepository


class MetadataEngine(FakeEngine):
    def review(self, current, question, turns):
        return dict(super().review(current, question, turns), coverage_gaps=['No regional field validation'],
                    model_metadata={'provider': 'fake', 'model': 'synthetic-v1'},
                    prompt_metadata={'version': 'review-v2', 'context_hash': 'synthetic'})


def test_review_metadata_and_complete_preview_are_audited_without_content_writes():
    repo = MemoryRepository()
    with TestClient(create_app(repo, FakeEvidence(), MetadataEngine({'title': 'Proposed title'}))) as client:
        record = client.app.state.service.create_requirement(fixture_draft(), 'contract-review')
        before = copy.deepcopy(repo.read()['requirements'])
        thread = create_thread(client, record['id'])
        run = ask(client, thread)
        assert run['state'] == 'succeeded'
        data = repo.read()
        turn = data['turns'][run['result_ids'][0]]
        assert turn['coverage_gaps'] == ['No regional field validation']
        assert turn['model_metadata']['model'] == 'synthetic-v1'
        assert turn['prompt_metadata']['version'] == 'review-v2'
        preview = turn['change_preview']
        assert preview['new_evidence']['value'] == record['evidence']['value']
        assert preview['new_score'] == turn['score_preview']
        assert preview['proposed_content']['title'] == 'Proposed title'
        assert preview['human_review_required'] is True
        assert preview['unresolved_checks']['reviewed_target_ids']
        completed = next(e for e in data['events'] if e['action'] == 'CHALLENGE_COMPLETED')
        assert completed['after']['prompt_metadata'] == turn['prompt_metadata']
        assert data['requirements'] == before


@pytest.mark.parametrize('field,value', [('coverage_gaps', [3]), ('coverage_gaps', [' ']), ('coverage_gaps', {}),
    ('model_metadata', []), ('prompt_metadata', {'value': float('nan')}), ('model_metadata', {'value': object()})])
def test_malformed_optional_engine_fields_fail_without_successful_turn(field, value):
    class BadEngine(FakeEngine):
        def review(self, current, question, turns):
            return dict(super().review(current, question, turns), **{field: value})
    repo = MemoryRepository()
    with TestClient(create_app(repo, FakeEvidence(), BadEngine())) as client:
        record = client.app.state.service.create_requirement(fixture_draft(), 'contract-review')
        thread = create_thread(client, record['id'])
        run = ask(client, thread)
        assert run['state'] == 'failed'
        assert repo.read()['turns'] == {}


def test_patch_preview_uses_authoritative_evidence_one_snapshot_and_no_writes():
    class ChangedEvidence(FakeEvidence):
        def resolve(self, draft):
            context = super().resolve(draft)
            if draft['title'] == 'Hypothetical':
                context['score_context']['severity_level'] = 4
                context['evidence_context']['assignment_reviews'] = [1]
            return context
    repo = ProbeRepository()
    with TestClient(create_app(repo, ChangedEvidence())) as client:
        record = client.app.state.service.create_requirement(fixture_draft(), 'contract-review')
        before = repo.read()
        repo.reads = 0
        body = {'requirement_id': record['id'], 'expected_revision': 1, 'patch': {'title': 'Hypothetical'}}
        response = client.post('/api/scoring/preview', json=body)
        assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
        assert repo.reads == 1
        preview = response.json()
        assert preview['new_score']['effective_score'] > record['score']['effective_score']
        assert preview['new_evidence']['value'] > record['evidence']['value']
        assert repo.read() == before
        body['expected_revision'] = 2
        assert client.post('/api/scoring/preview', json=body).status_code == 409
        assert repo.read() == before

# Backend handoff

Role 3's governance implementation has been reviewed against [its assignment](../roles/03_BACKEND_AND_GOVERNANCE.md), [the implementation plan](../IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md), and [the challenge specification](../CHALLENGE_SPECIFICATION.md). The backend supports validated drafts, guarded human decisions, immutable revisions, deterministic scoring, audited review applications, complete exports and reconstructable approved freezes. The acceptance matrix and corrective findings are in [BACKEND_REVIEW.md](BACKEND_REVIEW.md).

**Full sprint integration sign-off remains pending:** actual Role 1/2 adapters, source reconciliation, live generation, Docker deployment and Role 4's UI workflow have not been demonstrated. Synthetic tests establish backend behavior; they do not establish the validity of original BMW evidence.

## Entry points and contracts

Run `services.api:app`; `pipeline/07_pm_review_api.py` delegates to the same application. [BACKEND_RUNTIME.md](BACKEND_RUNTIME.md) documents startup and the tested runtime boundary. [OpenAPI](../contracts/openapi.json) and [the synthetic fixture](../contracts/fixture_case.json) describe the HTTP contract. Shared models include source/evidence, signal/draft, review, score, revision, audit and freeze contracts. Preserve original legacy payloads through the explicit import/reconciliation path; do not relabel legacy 0–10 scores as v1.

`GET /api/requirements` returns `{items,total,offset,ranking_id}` and caps each page at 200. Complete CSV/JSON export uses `/api/requirements/export`, independently of pagination. CSV maps actual backend names such as `finding_links` and `evidence_links` into the required BMW columns while preserving original fields. Detail, evidence, history, history download, sources/records/pages, signal/thread review, run status, preview and freeze endpoints are provided. `API_PREFIX` changes the new-contract prefix; root aliases preserve selected legacy URLs, not every historical schema.

Every edit/decision/application requires an expected revision, named PM actor and nonblank rationale. Body and route IDs must match. Invalid domain inputs return 422, stale revisions/baselines 409, missing entities 404 and unavailable dependencies 503. Patches cannot change server-owned status, calculated scores or revisions. Edits/applications produce `PM_REVIEW` and clear approval and old overrides; application never grants approval. Approval requires human source, target/milestone and assumption confirmations, current verified evidence and cited strategic assessment. The named PM mechanism is a prototype identity input, not enterprise authentication.

Freeze rechecks selected approved revisions and evidence, captures complete requirement/source/configuration/ranking/decision payloads, and includes the full audit prefix through its retained checkpoint. Missing reconstructable source snapshots block freeze. Engine-supplied assumption/target review states start pending; only explicit human review can establish acceptance/resolution. Later edits leave committed snapshots unchanged. The hash chain is tamper-evident relative to a retained checkpoint; checkpoint retention outside the database remains an operational responsibility.

## Adapter responsibilities

`create_app` accepts injected `evidence_provider`, `source_provider`, `engine`, `import_service`, driver and repository. `BACKEND_ADAPTER_FACTORY=module:function` loads a synchronous factory during lifespan, passing `driver` and `repository`; it returns a mapping of those four adapter components. Invalid factories fail startup rather than silently replacing integrations.

- Evidence: `resolve(draft)` returns verified/traceable flags, authoritative `score_context`, `evidence_context`, pinned `source_snapshots`, and `required_assumption_ids`. Counts must describe the actual issue/cohort, forecasts need sourced 2030 locators, and fixed normalization is stored in immutable baseline configuration. Required successor/powertrain proxy IDs must identify the specific assumptions the PM must accept. Generic unrelated assumptions do not satisfy that guard. Native studies require reviewed relevant mappings; opaque channel labels remain opaque.
- Generation/review: `analyze(scope)` produces validated drafts with stable semantic identity; `review(entity, question, prior_turns)` returns cited answers, visible tool records and optional allowed patches. Review citations must resolve to authoritative source references. Signal review uses the same injected engine boundary. Model calls run outside governance transactions.
- Import: `import_data(scope)` returns validated import results and provenance snapshots. Import/consolidation provenance is audited when the adapter supplies it. Source-provider reads and graph-reference verification have synthetic and isolated graph acceptance, but Role 1's actual graph schema still needs reconciliation.
- Progress: adapters may accept `progress_callback`; supplied stage/progress/cache-mode updates are validated. Background jobs support partial results, bounded analysis batches, shared admission and same-thread review serialization. Interrupted jobs recover truthfully as failed. Execution is in-process, not a durable distributed queue.

### Review output and previews

Role 2 returns `ReviewEngineResult`: nonblank `answer`, optional `citations`, `tool_records`, `patch`, `coverage_gaps` (nonblank strings), `model_metadata` and `prompt_metadata` (finite JSON objects). Missing optional fields default to empty collections/null for existing adapters. Unknown fields and malformed optional values fail the run without a successful turn. Include provider/model identifiers, prompt version and context hashes in the metadata objects as available; empty defaults mean metadata was not supplied, not that a live model was verified. The backend persists these objects with the turn and completed audit payload, and model/prompt metadata with the run. Adapter `patch` is the HTTP proposal's field diff; the plan's conceptual `proposed_patch` must be mapped to this field by Role 2.

`score_preview` retains its existing priority-result shape. `change_preview` adds proposed content, authoritative ECI (`new_evidence`), old/new score and ranks, rank movements, base revision/ranking ID, and descriptive unresolved checks. Human target/source confirmations and unresolved assumption acceptance remain required; a preview never grants review or approval. A review completed after a concurrent edit is retained with `stale=true`; its preview describes the original base snapshot and cannot be applied to the new revision.

`POST /api/scoring/preview` also accepts `{requirement_id, expected_revision, patch}` for the same complete change preview without writes. Invalid/missing expected revisions return 422; stale revisions or changed immutable baseline configuration return 409. The existing alternate-weight preview stays available. Proposed content follows actual edit/application semantics, retaining already resolved assumptions; applying clears approval and overrides and produces PM_REVIEW. Source/target confirmations must be supplied again on approval.

### Role 1 retrieval and import coordination

Role 1's retrieval adapter must expose `search_feedback(query, scope, limit=20)`, `get_source_record(record_id)`, `get_survey_facts(topic, scope)`, `get_sales_facts(scope, year=2030)`, `search_document_chunks(query, scope, document_kind=None, limit=6)`, and `get_comment_cohort_counts(scope)`. Role 2 consumes these interfaces for bounded retrieval; Role 3 consumes their authoritative results through `resolve(draft)` and wraps source browsing through `list_sources`, `get(kind, id)`, and `verify_reference`. Retrieval implementations are owned by Role 1, not added to backend services. Returned identities, original values/text, source versions/locators, applicability and explicit unknowns must reconcile with the shared evidence DTOs before integration.

**Atomic import acceptance remains pending.** The current `import_data(scope)` adapter executes outside the later backend provenance transaction. It must not be described as an atomic source-import/audit transaction. Role 1 and Role 3 must agree a transaction-aware import interface using the same injected Neo4j transaction and audit sink (which never independently commits). Conversion/validation can run before that transaction; source/consolidation writes and their provenance events must commit or roll back together. Actual schema reconciliation and injected audit-failure rollback proof are required at integration. The current backend's atomic provenance-result persistence alone does not meet that cross-role requirement.

The default runtime has no production evidence/generation/import implementation. A configured provider key alone does not install one. Source queries assume the documented graph schema; an empty result is not proof that BMW sources were imported.

## Remaining acceptance

1. Connect actual Role 1 evidence/import/source adapters and reconcile original feedback IDs, native study mappings, strategy passages, source snapshots and sourced 2030 forecasts. Preserve private data outside public commits.
2. Connect Role 2 generation/review, verify stable reruns and rejected/approved preservation with real source lineage, cited answers and visible tool records. Demonstrate live provider use and any cache behavior honestly.
3. Validate the configured Neo4j 5.20 Compose image, container build/health and Role 4 UI requests to `http://api:8000`. Local Homebrew Neo4j acceptance does not establish container compatibility.
4. Demonstrate the complete import→draft→edit/apply→review→approve→freeze→private export workflow and deliver the approved package with Role 5.

Final fresh-review verification passed 790 tests with real Neo4j enabled; measured statement coverage is 99.59% and branch coverage is 99.05%. See [BACKEND_REVIEW.md](BACKEND_REVIEW.md) for the measured component table, remaining coverage paths and integration blockers.
AST examination of **254 test functions** found no identical bodies after ignoring function names and docstrings. This is an exact-duplication check, not proof that all behavioral overlap is useful. Manual review retained unit/API/real-graph overlap because it checks different boundaries: formula/domain correctness, request serialization, transactional isolation and actual rollback. Negative type partitions and the 25 state/action combinations protect separate contract cases. The 1,000 scoring probes run within one seeded test rather than inflating the case count.

Measured actual Neo4j transactions: identical generation retry or repeated progress uses **10 integrity queries and zero materialization writes**; changed progress uses **12 queries**, including only its changed job and ledger. An unrelated five-revision history remains unchanged. Tampering with unrelated history still blocks a no-op retry without repair. API responses avoid duplicate ledger reads. Full locked graph-copy verification, whole-ledger serialization and ranking snapshots for exact active revision baselines remain deliberate prototype integrity costs; scalability is not established.
